Organic Panel Bible

How to build an interface that is grown, not built: crisp instruments held in a living frame. The frame is flesh, chitin and bone in one body, the screens are black smoked glass, and the keys are hard, dark and lit at their rims. This is the organic counterpart of the Analog Panel Bible.

Draft. This guide is a living document: the method behind organic interfaces is still being found, one study step at a time, and every new lesson is added here (owner, 2026-10-31: "it's in draft and we'll be adding to it as we discover the methodology behind organic ui"). The study's latest notes from the owner: build the body in layers (bone underneath, muscle over it, leather stretched over both, veins under the skin), sculpt it rather than placing shapes, blend the textures, make it wetter, and never use raw primitives.

Owner, 2026-10-31"Nah that's bad lol. Let's make a new design system for organic" · "The brood is overly simple. It's just metal with ameobas on top. Completely missing the zerg aesthetic"

This guide goes with the skill .claude/skills/blender-organic-panels, which holds the Blender procedure, and the study generator tools/blender/organic_study.py, which renders every image here. The direction comes from the owner's notes and two reference screenshots of a hive race's interface that are not committed: we take how it is built (its shapes, materials and light), never its art. Every shape, word and colour on this page is our own.

Rule 1

Never use raw primitives

The owner, 2026-10-31: "I don't like the pubbles and the white tendril. These look like low effort shapes. Whereas the organic leather frame looks a little more purposeful and organic", and "never use raw primitives".

  • No raw primitive is ever a visible form. No sphere, capsule, cylinder, cone, torus, plain tube or smooth untextured spike appears in a render as itself: not a bead, a pustule, a spine, a claw, a rib or a tendril.
  • Every form is sculpted into the one body and carries its skin detail. A bead row becomes vertebrae under the skin; a spine becomes a bone crest the skin thins over; a pustule becomes a swelling in the leather with light glowing through it; a tendril becomes a sinew cord raised under the skin. Pores, wrinkles, veins and wetness run over all of it.
  • Primitives may only be invisible construction: metaball seeds, cutters and the shapes a height field is computed from, which the sculpt and its remesh absorb so no trace of them survives.
  • The crisp instruments (the screen glass, the key caps, the portrait) are tech, not body, and keep their clean edges (chapter 4).
Rule 2

Layered anatomy, sculpted

The owner, 2026-10-31: "Your approach used discrete shapes. The zerg have a couple layers. There's a bone underneath. The leather stretches over muscle and bone with veins underneath. One thing you could try is sculpting. Try sculpting these shapes and render them. Try blending different textures together. And make the material a little more wet looking."

A frame is built the way a sculptor builds a body: from the inside out, as layers of one surface, never as parts placed side by side.

  1. Bone. The armature: a ridge round every opening, a spine along the top with vertebrae of different sizes, each turned its own way, a blade-like crest on each and a shadowed hollow between each pair; ribs off a side; an arch over the portrait; horn crests that reach past the frame; claws under the key shelf (step 16).
  2. Muscle. Swollen bundles beside and between the bones, following the frame's direction, lumpy along their run and striated along it; sinew cords running from panel to panel; a cradle for the crystal (step 17).
  3. Skin. One leather surface stretched over both: tight over every crest, so the skin is thin there and the bone shows through, stained ivory blended into the leather; bridging the gaps between crests as webs in tension, which wrinkle; diving steeply into every opening (step 18).
  4. Under the skin. Veins raised under it, dark purple-blue through it; sacs of light swelling it, glowing green through the stretched skin; creases sunk at the foot of every ridge (step 19).
  5. Blend the materials by the sculpt (step 20) and wet it where flesh is wet (step 21): the masks come from the layers themselves (below).

How it is sculpted, headless

The frame is a height field, z = h(x, y), computed in numpy by tools/blender/organic_anatomy.py and written into a dense grid mesh (one sample every 0.5 mm, one per pixel at 2 px per mm). Every form rises from whatever lies under it (bone from the floor, muscle from the bone, cords from the muscle), so nothing stands on a cliff. The skin is the smooth maximum of bone and muscle, then the larger of that plus 0.9 mm and a 6 mm blur of it less 0.6 mm: the blur bridges the gaps as webs, the maximum keeps the skin tight on every crest. The coordinates the frame is computed in are warped by two octaves of noise, so no ridge runs parallel to a rectangle for long.

Why a height field

Every kit piece is rendered face on, so a surface that never folds under itself loses nothing a captain can see, and it is exactly repeatable from the script. Scripted sculpt-mode strokes (bpy.ops.sculpt with context overrides) need a window context headless Blender does not give and drift with brush settings between versions; a skin shrinkwrapped on a remeshed union bridges gaps poorly and keeps the union's seams. The field gives the layers for free: the masks below are differences between them.

Masks from the sculpt

Bone shows where the skin is thinnest over a bone that stands proud of its own surroundings, in patches the leather still clings to. Muscle shows raw and red where it bulges above the bone. Veins are their own paths. Creases are where the skin is concave. Webs are where the skin bridges a gap. Sacs are their own swellings. Depth is the height, for the cavern's fall into shadow. Each is written to the mesh as a colour attribute and read by one material.

Chapter 1

One organism

An organic console is not a set of panels with growth added. It is one creature that holds instruments. Three ideas follow from that, and every later chapter is one of them in practice:

  1. The frame and the backdrop are the same body. Panels are swellings in one ribbed wall of tissue; tubes, veins and ribs run from one to the next. There is no black gap between panels, and no panel floats.
  2. The tech is crisp, the frame is soft. The parts a captain reads or presses (screens, keys, the portrait) are hard-edged, dark and clean. Everything round them is curved, wet and uneven. The contrast between the two is the look.
  3. The body breaks the rectangle; the instruments do not. Spines, horns and arches grow past a panel's edge and over its neighbours, but every screen and key face stays an exact, measured rectangle that nothing covers.
Chapter 2

Five materials

The whole look is five materials. Each has one job, and none is grey metal. From step 20 the body's three (flesh, bone, muscle) are one material blended by the sculpt's masks, not separate objects: bone is where the skin thins over a crest, never a white object laid on top (rules 1 and 2).

Flesh

The frame and the wall. Dark maroon-brown, leathery: fine pores and diagonal creases in the bump, its colour stepped by its own ambient occlusion (black in the folds, lit brown on the swells), a little subsurface so thin edges warm up, and a satin wet coat.

base #33110f · lit #6a2620 · fold #080303 · roughness 0.62 · coat 0.55 at 0.22 · subsurface 0.08 over 1.5 mm

Chitin

First round only (steps 3-14); a placed plate is banned by rule 1. Hard dark armour now comes from bone crests under the skin. The armour: segmented plates along a frame's top and shoulders, overlapping like vertebrae and sunk into the flesh so it swells round each one. Near black and hard, its shape carried by one sharp highlight under a clear coat, with a faint thin-film sheen.

base #140c0e to #4a3236 by noise · roughness 0.3 · coat 1.0 at 0.03 · thin film 380 nm

Bone

Spines, horns, claws, vertebrae and arches, as crests of the bone layer the skin thins over: stained ivory, worn brighter where the crest is highest, blended into the leather in patches, never a separate white object (rule 1).

from step 20: stained #7d6b4c to ivory #cfc2a2 by fine noise · where the skin is under 0.9-2.3 mm over a crest standing 2.5 mm proud of its 5 mm surroundings · in patches (broad noise above 0.3) · roughness 0.48-0.73, drier than the flesh

Muscle and veins

Raw sinew where muscle bulges through in the hollows: redder and wetter than the leather. Veins under the skin: dark purple-blue showing through it.

muscle #62140f (dark step #4a0f0c), 75% · veins #1c1028, 80% · creases #080303, 75%, with dried fluid #3a2c14 in their patches

Smoked glass

Every screen: a recess of near-black glass, glossy, with faint dark-red veins only at its edges, held by a thin bronze rim. The content glows on the black.

#050405 · roughness 0.12 · coat 1.0 · veins #3a0d0c outside 45% of a squarish oval · rim bronze #9a5a34, metal

Light

Things that glow: the readouts (pale green), the key rims and icons (our amber), the pustules (green, life), the crystal (violet, the heart). Light is never a surface colour of the frame.

readout #b8f27a · accent #ffb03a · life #6fd82a · hero #b35cff

Chapter 3

Form: grow it, don't cut it

Hard-surface panels are cut: a plate, a boolean, a bevel. Organic panels are grown: soft elements that merge wherever they meet, so one shape flows into the next with no seam.

  • Metaballs, then a remesh. Capsules hug each opening (thicker along the top, thinner below: the thick-and-thin rhythm), balls swell at the corners, negative cubes carve the openings. The metaball is converted to a mesh, voxel remeshed at 1.4 mm, lumped by a 2.2 mm cloud displacement and relaxed by corrective smoothing.
  • A ribcage rhythm. Short capsules laid across a frame's sides, longest in the middle and tapering at the ends, turn a tube into a ribbed thing. The wall behind is the same: ribs sweeping across every 24 mm, bowed and uneven.
  • Armour sunk, not stuck. Chitin plates overlap each other and sit half inside the flesh. A plate standing on a frame reads as a bean on a sausage (step 5 shows both).
  • Asymmetry. The left side carries the long canopy spines; the right side has short swept-back spines. A grown thing is never mirrored.
  • Past the edge. Arches, canopies and horns rise above a panel's top and over its neighbour. That is what makes the silhouette alive.
Chapter 4

Crisp tech in a soft frame

What the captain reads and presses is the one place nothing is soft.

  • Screens are black. A smoked recess sunk 6 mm into the body, the readout glowing on it. A lit field behind dark letters (version 23's lime screens) is low contrast and fights every glow on the console.
  • A calm middle. The glass's veins live only near its rim; a squarish oval over the readout is plain black, so the letters sit on nothing.
  • Keys are square, dark and lit at the rim. A near-black cap with a small round, a thin glowing amber rim inset 2.5 mm, and a clean amber icon. It sits in a pit grown in the flesh. Soft green pillows read as more growth, not as something to press.
  • A press pushes the cap in. The cap sinks 3 mm and drops 2 mm; its rim and icon brighten; the flesh round it stays put (step 13).
  • The portrait lives in a pocket. A tall dark pocket under an arch of flesh, the face lit from below out of the dark. A flat name bar reads as a label, not a presence.
Chapter 5

Light

  • A warm key light from above, large and soft (an area light 180 mm wide, 420 mm up). It puts a wet highlight on every ridge's top and leaves the hollows under ribs and plates deep.
  • Two grazing rims from the sides, warm on the left and faintly violet on the right, at 30% and 20% of the key. They light the edges of the bone and the wet flesh, which is what makes a surface read as wet.
  • A dim cool fill from below, 3% of the key, only so the darkest folds are not pure black.
  • Bioluminescent accents light their surroundings. Each pustule has a tiny point light just in front of it, so the flesh round it picks up green. The crystal has one inside and one spilling below it.
  • Never a flat front light. Step 1 to 4 use one; step 5 shows the difference.
Chapter 6

Palette and value

Version 23 used several mid hues at one value (grey, olive, lime), mottled together: it read as camouflage. The fix is few hues on a value ladder: the wall darkest, flesh dark, chitin dark with bright highlights, bone pale, and the light brightest. Each colour that glows has one meaning.

Fold#080303 · hollows, pits
Flesh#33110f · frame, wall
Lit flesh#6a2620 · swells
Chitin#140c0e · armour
Bone#e2d6bb · spines, horns
Screen#050405 · glass
Bronze#9a5a34 · screen rims
Readout#b8f27a · text on glass
Accent#ffb03a · keys only
Life#6fd82a · pustules, health
Hero#b35cff · the crystal only

Green is a light, never a surface. The amber accent is ours (the reference uses its own hot colour for keys); violet belongs to the hero alone.

Chapter 7

Fit rules, measured

Growth may cover a frame, a bezel or a neighbour's frame. It may never cover what a captain reads or presses. The study measures it on the geometry: every vertex of every growing object that stands in front of the screen glass is projected onto the view, and its distance to each protected rectangle is taken. The sculpted surface is measured on its height field: every sample standing above the glass. Step 24's skin dives into each opening so that it is below the glass 2.6 mm before the rectangle's edge; the first round's canopy came within 0.09 mm of the portrait window.

RuleWhat it saysHow it is checked
G1No growth covers a screen, a key face or the portrait window, with at least 2 mm to spare.Nearest growth in front of the glass to each protected rectangle is 2 mm or more (organic_study.py measure, measure_field).
G2Children stay inside their parents: a readout inside its screen, an icon inside its key, the face inside its pocket.Laid out from the protected rectangle with a margin; the kit's console_fit measures the page.
G3Overhangs never cover another panel's content: a canopy may pass over a neighbour's frame, never its screen.G1 run against every panel's rectangles, not only its own.
G4A 9-slice piece keeps its growth in the corners and edges; the stretching middle is plain flesh, so it stretches without smearing a rib.Margins chosen round the ribs, as in the analog kits.
Protected rectangleClearanceNearest growthResult

Chapter 8

Blender recipes

The sculpt and its material (step 16 on) are the method. The first round's recipes below them (metaball body, ribs, chitin plates, bone curves, pustule spheres) are kept as a record; every one that places a visible primitive is banned by rule 1.

The sculpt

organic_anatomy.Sculpt: a 0.5 mm grid. Bone: rings 13-15 mm outside each opening, 6-7 mm wide, 10-13 mm high, on coordinates warped 9 mm (34 mm noise) + 3 mm (11 mm noise); the spine a 12 mm ridge 14 mm high with vertebrae every 18-29 mm, 0.7-1.4 x, ellipses 13-18 x 8-12 mm turned up to 28 degrees, a 3 x 9 mm crest blade to 21 mm; ribs 3.2 mm, tapering; the portrait arch 6.5 mm, 15 mm high; horn crests 6-7 mm to 14-16 mm. Muscle: a mass 28-38 mm round each opening rising to 3-11 mm (26 mm noise); bundles 11-12 mm and 27-31 mm out, 8-14 mm wide, to 12 mm, striated every 2.3 mm; cords 4-6 mm raised 2 x their radius. Skin: max(core + 0.9, blur(core, 6 mm) - 0.6), blurred 0.6 mm. Veins: 26 seeded walks, 4 mm steps, 0.7-1.3 mm, raised 0.7 mm. Sacs: raised 7 mm x bell^1.3. Creases: the Laplacian of the 1.2 mm-blurred skin, sunk 0.5 mm. Openings: z = min(z, -14 + 5 (d - 2.6)).

The blended material

One Principled; colour attributes m1 (bone, muscle, vein) and m2 (crease, web, sac, depth). Leather: ramp #080303 / #2e140d / #55281a on AO (10 mm) + 0.3 x broad noise. Then muscle, veins, bone (in patches), creases and dried fluid mixed in by their masks; the sacs' emission green x sac^0.9, broken by the veins over them; depth to black, (1 - depth)^0.7. Bump 0.8 over 0.7 mm: Voronoi pores (scale 520) + wave wrinkles x (0.25 + 1.2 x web) + grain. Wet (step 21): coat 0.12 + 0.6 muscle + 0.8 crease - 0.5 bone, coat roughness 0.08 + 0.4 x fine noise, roughness 0.48 + 0.25 bone, subsurface 0.12.

Keys, hot

From step 23 the rims and icons are #ff8400 at emission 1.8: AgX turns a bright orange pale and pink as it drives it harder (step 14's peach), so the accent is a saturated orange driven gently, its brightness carried by the dark round it.

The crystal, frosted

Shards cut uneven (each cone subdivided twice, its vertices pushed 0.7-1.25 x across and 4% along, flat shaded), #4c2490, roughness 0.5, transmission 1, coat 0.5 at 0.35, a 0.3 mm frost bump; a core of light inside each (emission 6); a 46 mm sphere of violet volume, density 0.6, as mist.

The body (first round)

Metaball, threshold 0.6, resolution 1.8 mm. Capsules round each opening (radius 22 mm on top, 18 on the sides, 18 below), balls at the corners at 1.25 x. Negative cubes, stiffness 10, carve the openings 3 mm larger than their rectangles. Convert to mesh; squash the back to 20%; Remesh, voxel 1.4 mm; Displace, clouds 18 mm, 2.2 mm; Corrective Smooth, 5 iterations; shade smooth.

Ribs

Capsules, radius 7-7.5 mm, length 14-22 mm (a sine across the run), turned 12-15 degrees, set 4-6 mm proud. The wall: tubes of radius 7.5-10 mm every 24 mm, bowed by a sine of 7 mm.

Flesh shader

Principled. Colour ramp fold #080303 at 0.3, flesh #33110f at 0.75, lit #6a2620 at 1.15, driven by AO (14 mm) + 0.3 x noise (scale 260, detail 10). Bump 0.5 over 0.6 mm from wave bands (scale 90, distortion 18) + noise. Roughness 0.62, coat 0.55 at 0.22, subsurface 0.08 random walk over 1.5 mm.

Chitin plates

UV spheres squashed to 15.5 x 13 x 6.5 mm, swelling 18% to the middle of a run, overlapping by a third, tilted -22 degrees and -18 degrees, half sunk. Shader: noise between #140c0e and #4a3236, roughness 0.3, coat 1.0 at 0.03, thin film 380 nm.

Bone

Bezier curves, bevel depth 3-10 mm, taper by point radius from 1.0 at the root to 0.05 at the tip. Shader ivory #e2d6bb, AO ramp to #8a7a5e at the root, roughness 0.38, coat 0.5, subsurface 0.15.

Smoked screen

A recess 6 mm into the body. Glass #050405, roughness 0.12, coat 1. Voronoi distance-to-edge (scale 30, width 0.03) for veins in #3a0d0c, masked by (dx/rx)^4 + (dy/ry)^4 from 0.45 to 1. Bronze rim: a 1.6 mm tube 4.5 mm outside the rectangle, corners 4 mm.

Keys

A box with a 2 mm, 4-segment bevel, #0e0a0b, roughness 0.28, coat 1. A 0.7 mm tube rim 2.5 mm inside the face, emission amber 1.6 (3.2 pressed). Flat icon polygons on the face, same emission. A point light 12 mm out, 0.012 W (0.03 pressed). Pressed: back 3 mm, down 2 mm.

Glow

Pustules: spheres, emission 0.8 with subsurface 0.5, and a point light of 0.012 W per mm of radius just in front. The crystal: hexagonal cones (a tip and a short root), transmission 0.6, emission 0.6 violet, a 0.3 W point inside and 0.25 W below.

Render

Cycles, CPU, 32 samples, denoised, AgX with medium-high contrast. Orthographic face on, 2 px per mm. World near black (#010101).

Chapter 9

What went wrong in v23

Version 23 rebuilt the Vhorr Brood as "assimilated tech": a captured machine with growth over it. The owner's verdict was that it was "just metal with ameobas on top". Compared element by element with the reference, in our own words:

ElementVersion 23What it should beStep
MaterialGrey stone and metal with lime moss blotchesLeathery maroon-brown flesh and near-black chitin with a wet sheen, ivory bone. No grey base; green only as light3
FormFlat, even-width rounded rectanglesThick sculpted carapace, ribbed like a ribcage, a vertebral band along the top, asymmetric2, 4
SilhouetteInside the panel's boxHorns and spines arching over the panels, a canopy over the portrait, growing past the top edge9
ScreensLit lime fields behind dark text, low contrastNear-black smoked recesses with a thin bronze rim; the content glows on black6
KeysSoft green pillowsSquare dark caps with glowing amber rims and clean icons, set into the flesh7
Name plateA flat green barA tall fleshy pocket under an arch holding a live portrait8
JoinsSeparate boxes on blackOne continuous ribbed wall of tissue; tubes, veins and ribs between the panels10
HeroA small egg in a grey discA big faceted violet crystal, the console's heartbeat12
LightFlat and evenWarm key from above, deep hollows, wet highlights on ridges, glowing accents5, 11
PaletteGrey and lime everywhereDark flesh, ivory bone, black screens, one amber accent for keys, green for life, violet for the hero3, 6, 11

The root cause was the premise: starting from a machine and adding growth made the growth decoration. Starting from the creature and letting it hold the machine (chapter 1) fixes all ten at once.

Chapter 10

Worked example

One corner of a console, built up in twenty-four steps by tools/blender/organic_study.py. Each step changes one thing and keeps every change before it. Steps 1-14 are the first round; steps 15-24 are the second, after the owner's notes on it (rules 1 and 2).

1 · Version 23's way

A grey plate with the openings cut by booleans, rivets, lime moss blobs, a lit lime screen with dark text, green pillow keys, a flat green name bar and a small egg in a disc.

Lesson: growth added to a machine is decoration. Chapter 1.

2 · One sculpted body

The plate became one metaball body grown round every opening, the neighbour panel's frame part of the same body. Still grey, so only the form changed.

Lesson: grow, don't cut. Chapter 3.

3 · Flesh and chitin, not stone

Leathery maroon-brown flesh with pores, creases and a wet coat; a band of near-black chitin plates sunk along the top and down the portrait's shoulder.

Lesson: the material is most of the look. Chapter 2.

4 · A ribcage rhythm

Ribs across the screen frame's sides, longest in the middle; ribs down the portrait pocket; short ribs under the key shelf.

Lesson: repetition with variation reads as anatomy. Chapter 3.

5 · Warm light from above

The flat front light became a warm soft key from above, two grazing rims and a dim cool fill. The flesh turned wet, the hollows deep.

Lesson: wetness is a highlight on a ridge against a dark hollow. Chapter 5.

6 · Screens are black smoked glass

The lime field became a near-black glass recess with a thin bronze rim, its veins only at the edges; the readout glows on it.

Lesson: content glows on black; a lit field behind text loses contrast. Chapter 4.

7 · Crisp keys set into the flesh

The green pillows became square dark caps with glowing amber rims and clean icons, each in a pit grown in the flesh.

Lesson: the parts you press are tech, crisp and hard. Chapter 4.

8 · A portrait pocket under an arch

The flat name bar became a tall dark pocket under a bow of flesh, a face lit from below inside it, its name glowing at its foot.

Lesson: the captain's officer is a presence, not a label.

9 · Bone spines arching over

Two long ivory spines rise behind the portrait and arch over it and the screen's corner; short swept-back spines off the right; claws curl under the key shelf.

Lesson: the silhouette breaks the rectangle; the instruments do not. Chapter 3.

10 · One wall of tissue

The black backdrop became a ribcage wall of the same flesh, darker; tubes and veins run between the panels, half sunk; a tendril reaches the neighbour, thick at its roots, thin and knotted between.

Lesson: no panel floats. Chapter 1.

11 · Green for life only

Pustules at the joints glow green from inside and light the flesh round them. Green appears nowhere else as a surface.

Lesson: each glowing colour has one meaning. Chapter 6.

12 · A crystal heart

A cluster of faceted violet shards in a cradle of flesh above the neighbour panel, lit from inside, spilling violet below.

Lesson: one big focal object gives the console a heartbeat.

13 · Pressed

The middle key pressed: its cap sinks 3 mm and drops 2 mm, its rim and icon brighten, and the flesh round it stays put.

Lesson: the inner part moves, the frame never does (version 20's rule).

14 · Final, measured

All of it, with the fit measured: no growth covers the screen, a key face or the portrait window (chapter 7).

Lesson: a living frame still obeys the kit's rules, by measurement.

15 · Nothing placed on the body

Step 14 with every placed primitive taken away: the bead row, the chitin plates, the white spines and claws, the green spheres, the wall's tubes. What is left is the leather frame the owner liked.

Lesson: the placed shapes were decoration; the sculpted frame carries the look. Rule 1.

16 · Sculpt the bone first

The first round's body is gone. A height field holds only the bone layer: rings round the openings, the spine with its vertebrae, ribs, the portrait arch, horn crests and claws, shown as pale clay on dark.

Lesson: the armature decides the silhouette before any flesh exists. Rule 2.

17 · Muscle over the bone

Muscle rises from the bone: lumpy bundles round each opening, striated along their run, cords to the neighbour and to the edges, the crystal's cradle. Red clay over the pale bone.

Lesson: the swell between the bones is what makes a frame read as alive. Rule 2.

18 · Skin stretched over both

One leather surface over both: tight on every crest, webbed across the gaps, diving into every opening. One plain leather material.

Lesson: a single draped surface ties every form into one body. Rule 2.

19 · Veins, cords and sacs under the skin

Veins raised under the skin, creases sunk at the foot of every ridge, and sacs swelling it with green light glowing through.

Lesson: what lies under the skin is shown by the skin, never stuck on it.

20 · Blend the materials by the sculpt

Bone shows through where the skin is thinnest over a crest, raw muscle in the hollows, veins dark through the skin, grime and dried fluid in the creases, all from masks the sculpt wrote.

Lesson: the layers give the materials their places; nothing is painted by hand.

21 · Wet where flesh is wet

Wettest in the creases and on the muscle, drier on bone, the coat's roughness broken by fine noise so the highlight breaks up over pores and wrinkles.

Lesson: wet is a broken highlight in the hollows, not a glossy shell.

22 · A cavern behind, not a wall

The flat backdrop became a ribcage receding into the dark: ribs and a spine column of the same sculpt, falling into shadow with depth.

Lesson: depth behind the panels makes the console sit inside the creature.

23 · Dark, so the instruments carry the light

The light dropped to 70%; the key rims became a hot saturated orange; the crystal frosted, uneven and lit from a core inside, with a breath of mist.

Lesson: the frame is dark so the screens, keys and the heart carry the light.

24 · Final, layered and measured

All of it at final quality, with the fit measured: the skin is below the glass at least 2 mm before every screen, key face and the portrait window (chapter 7).

Lesson: a sculpted frame still obeys the kit's rules, by measurement.

Chapter 11

Before you call it done

  • No raw primitive is a visible form anywhere on the body (rule 1).
  • The frame is sculpted as layers, bone, muscle and skin, and the bone shows only through thin skin (rule 2).
  • No grey metal anywhere; the frame is flesh and bone, and the backdrop is the same body.
  • Every panel joins its neighbours through the wall: ribs, tubes or tendrils, no black gaps.
  • Something grows past the top edge; the left and right are not mirrored.
  • Every screen is black glass with a thin rim and a calm middle; text glows on it.
  • Every key is a crisp dark cap with a lit rim and a clean icon, set into the flesh; pressing moves only the cap.
  • Green is only light for life; the key accent appears only on keys; violet only on the hero.
  • The light comes from above; hollows are deep; ridges show a wet highlight.
  • G1 to G4 pass, measured, and the kit's fit checks pass on the page.
  • Look at a 2x crop of every key, screen and the portrait before calling it done.
